text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli army begins Hebron redeployment. Knesset OKs Hebron pact.
- Dor Energy signs $400 million deal with Polish state oil company Centrala Produktow Nastowysh to construct 400 petrol stations in Poland over the next five years.
- Japanese firm likely to cancel $250 million industrial and tourism investment in Omer, southern Israeli town.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel: We'll take actions to offset flow arising from purchase of foreign currency.
- Globes poll shows improvement in image of Finance Minister Dan Meridor: 47 percent say he is strong, 46 percent weak.
- Israel raises $750 million in United States in framework of U.S. guarantees at interest rate of 7.052 percent.
MAARIV
- Israeli army leaves Hebron.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visits United States -- in mid-February.

- Gallup poll of 509 Jews shows rise in Israeli support for Hebron deal: 57 percent for (compared with 55 percent two weeks ago), 19 percent against (compared with 27 percent), 19 percent don't know, 5 percent have no response.

- Palestinian negotiator Abu Mazen, asked if he could see Netanyahu signing an agreement to create an independent Palestinian state, says: "I believe that sooner or later he will reach this conclusion. He will understand a Palestinian state doesn't endanger anyone but will contribute to stability in the region."
HAARETZ
- U.S. President Bill Clinton asks Netanyahu to renew peace talks on the Israeli-Syrian track.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor prepared a resignation letter a week ago, following the appointment, later retracted, of lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney general.
- Hebron evacuation gives stock market a 3 percent boost in two days.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Concern in army intelligence that Syria will go to war because of freeze on diplomatic front.
- Poll shows surge in Israeli army motivation: 64 percent of youth -- compared with 59 percent in 1995 -- believe those with a combat profile should serve in battle units.
YERUSHALAYIM
- Jerusalem municipality threatens to seize Netanyahu's bank account for nonpayment of water bills on family residence.
